gloss: to be on good terms; to be close; to get along well

definitions.gloss: to be on good terms; to be close friends; to get along well
definitions.explanation: Describes a relationship where two or more people have a warm, friendly connection and enjoy each other's company.

examples.japanese: あの{二人|ふたり}は{仲|なか}が{良|よ}い。
examples.english: Those two are on good terms.

examples.japanese: {隣|となり}の{家族|かぞく}とは{仲|なか}が{良|よ}くて、よく{一緒|いっしょ}にバーベキューをする。
examples.english: We get along well with the family next door and often have barbecues together.

examples.japanese: {兄弟|きょうだい}の{仲|なか}が{良|よ}いのは{親|おや}にとってうれしいことだ。
examples.english: It makes parents happy when siblings get along well.

notes:
A fundamental expression for describing interpersonal relationships. Often written as {仲|なか}がいい in casual contexts. The opposite is {仲|なか}が{悪|わる}い (to be on bad terms).

USAGE:
Often modifies nouns: {仲|なか}の{良|よ}い{友達|ともだち} (a close friend). Can also be used predicatively: {仲|なか}が{良|よ}い (they get along well). The colloquial form uses いい instead of {良|よ}い.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {仲|なか}の{良|よ}い{友達|ともだち}: a close friend
- {仲|なか}{良|よ}くする: to get along with, to be friendly
- {仲|なか}{良|よ}く{暮|く}らす: to live harmoniously
- {仲|なか}が{良|よ}さそう: they seem to get along well

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {親|した}しい: close, intimate — describes the depth of a relationship
- {気|き}が{合|あ}う: to hit it off — emphasizes compatibility
- {仲|なか}が{悪|わる}い: to be on bad terms — the opposite expression
